title: Modded logistics recipes were omitted when names did not match fixed tiers

failing_environment.reported_behavior: Additional transport-belt tiers did not receive Belt Productivity when their recipe names were outside MIR's reviewed fixed lists.

reproduction.result: Name-bound tiers omitted structurally valid final logistics prototypes. C29 discovers opaque recipe and item names through final place_result entity types while preserving explicit productivity denials and reviewed-family precedence.

root_cause.summary: Belt and inserter compatibility relied on explicit recipe families and recognizable names rather than the final produced item's place_result entity prototype type.

regression_propositions: opaque modded belt and inserter names are classified by final place_result entity type
transport-belt, underground-belt, splitter, lane-splitter, loader, loader-1x1, and inserter entity types are covered
reviewed family attachments replace weaker structural fallback membership without duplicate effects
allow_productivity false, maximum_productivity zero, recycling, and productive self-return recipes remain excluded
the AdvancedBeltsSA adapter fixture observes all twelve expected belt-family effects and four productivity-ignored fluid returns
the exact C29 AAI loader, semantic-family, synthetic-scale, and randomized-order runtime scenarios pass
the item prototype index and recipe fact index build once and each stream match identity computes at most once

closure.proof_required: complete C29 ecosystem and performance evaluation, exact manual acceptance, protected qualification, verified seal, promotion, and published 3.2.3 bytes
